items.prompt: To rewrite a fraction like this 7/10. With a hundred on the bottom… 7/10 = ▢/100 We just multiply the top and bottom by ten.
Watch what I change. 3/10 Again I multiply top and bottom by ten.
Watch what I change again. 9/10 Again, top and bottom by ten.
items.demo: *90/100*. Each time, we multiply by ten over ten 10/10, which is a fraction equal to one.

items.prompt: Your turn. Rewrite four tenths 4/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 100.
Rewrite six tenths 6/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 100.
Rewrite one tenth 1/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 100.
Rewrite twelve tenths 12/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 100.
Rewrite ten tenths 10/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 100.
Rewrite seven tenths 7/10 as an equivalent fraction with a bottom value of 1000.
Sam says 7/10 becomes 7/100 because we just add a zero to the bottom. Is Sam right? How do you know?
items.demo: *No*. We must multiply top and bottom by the same number, or the value changes. 7/100 is smaller than 7/10.
